source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Stop all antiseizure medication immediately because every agent carries the same fetal risk","B":"Arrange preconception review because fetal risks vary by drug, and do not stop therapy abruptly","C":"Continue the current regimen without discussion because pregnancy does not affect treatment choices","D":"Avoid folic acid because supplementation is contraindicated with antiseizure medication therapy"}}
source_row.rationale: Current AAN/AES/SMFM guidance emphasizes optimizing antiseizure therapy before pregnancy when possible, balancing seizure control with medication-specific fetal risks, and using folic acid. Abrupt discontinuation can endanger the patient and fetus.
source_row.source_detail: Practice Guideline, May 2024: teratogenesis, perinatal and neurodevelopmental outcomes; folic acid and medication selection; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: AAN/AES/SMFM — Antiseizure Medication Exposure in Pregnancy Guideline
source_row.stem: A client taking an antiseizure medication plans pregnancy. Which teaching is most appropriate?
